message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The gene responsible for mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion—if a male lion inherits at least one copy of the allele that promotes mane growth, it will typically develop a mane. This trait is not expressed in females (they lack the Y chromosome that carries the gene), so the presence of a mane is a clear example of a dominant trait in the species.
